title: Breakfast Under the Legionlance: The Speaker on Markop’s Back, a Maid Without a Name, and a Daycare Vote
subtitle: Waluigi’s Cut — black bread with an Imperial seal, a pen in the dark, a Speaker carried through town, and the loudest breakfast nobody finished resolving
filed: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — the screening desk, watching the morning account; exact hour unrecorded
pullQuote: HOW ABOUT WE DON’T? THE SHIP IS STILL OUTSIDE.
standfirst: The projector rolls the morning account in order. Waluigi is at the screening desk with one hand on PAUSE, live-reacting as Remi and Archie debate the ship, Markop’s blackout sequence plays once, and a two-course breakfast turns into a contest over who gets to speak for the Toads. The image stays on the screen; no later outcome is supplied.

sections.heading: ROLL THE TAPE: THE MENU HAS AN IMPERIAL SEAL
sections.body:
The projector is warm, the morning account is on the screen, and Waluigi has one hand on PAUSE because the first object in frame is black bread stamped with the Imperial seal. Breakfast has opened with a state emblem. Waluigi has opened with a question: is the bread trying to make a point, or does the kitchen have a very serious stamp? Either way, the bread is dense, the butter is clarified and measured, the mountain trout is smoked and thin, and the root relish is pickled. The tea is strong, stewed long, and served in heavy cups. No sugar unless somebody asks in writing. Waluigi is delighted that the sugar has a paperwork requirement. Nobody has even ordered the political argument yet and the tea already has terms.

Remi looks at the menu and asks, “How do you think we're going to take our ship back from the Toads?” Waluigi stops the frame on the word “our.” A ship can be a lot of things; at this exact breakfast it is also a disputed noun. Archie offers the strategy: “I think there's a good strategy we could use. How about we don't?” Waluigi lets the silence after that line run for a second. It is a full plan, grammatically complete, and absolutely not what the person holding the menu asked for.

Remi points out, “We still have the power stick,” meaning X.O.’s staff. Archie does not encourage a dramatic wave. He warns her, “First things first: if you're going to wave that around and use it, try to be careful with it.” Then he lowers his voice: “I've seen that staff's power. It has catastrophic consequences. We don't want to turn this place we're in into a nice—”

The line ends there. Waluigi reaches for the remote, not the staff. Nobody uses it in this scene. The screen holds on breakfast and the unfinished sentence, and Waluigi refuses to supply the ending. A pause is not permission to invent a crater. WAH.

BLACK BREAD. IMPERIAL SEAL. CLARIFIED BUTTER. SMOKED TROUT. PICKLED ROOT. STRONG TEA. Waluigi is counting the menu items because the projector is currently showing a committee meeting disguised as breakfast.

sections.heading: STOP THE TAPE: MARKOP AND RIVERS LOSE THE LIGHTS
sections.body:
The picture cuts away from the stall and into the earlier encounter. Markop tells Rivers, “The Legion—my friends.” Rivers asks, “So you're a Legionary now?” Waluigi turns toward the audience. That is not what Markop said. The Legion is his friends; there is a difference between a uniform and a person you care about, and Rivers has stepped directly on the difference with a question mark.

Markop says Rivers still hurt people, including “that one guy.” Rivers goes at him with a pen, trips, and the lights go out. Waluigi points at the screen. A pen. A trip. A blackout. This scene has taken the most ordinary object on a desk and promoted it to the opening move of a dark-room confrontation. “Whoa. Someone turned off the lights.” Correct. That is the room’s current condition, not a metaphor Waluigi is going to decorate.

Markop thinks he cannot kill Rivers in the dark without dishonor. Rivers laughs: “All according to plan. You can't kill me—it's dishonorable now.” Waluigi puts the remote down. Rivers has found a loophole in the rules of a fight by falling over in the dark, and now he is explaining the loophole while tripping again into Markop’s arms. Markop hogties him.

“Unhand me, you horse!” Rivers says. Waluigi makes the exact face of a man who has just watched someone get tied up and immediately complain about the transportation options. Markop says, “Time to bring you to justice,” then looks around and notices the Toads are gone. Waluigi scans the empty parts of the frame. They were there; now they are not. No explanation arrives with the pen.

Markop asks, “What's your real goal, Speaker Rivers?” Rivers starts with “My goal? What do you mean?” and then stumbles through “It's to protect the world from devastation—to un—it's to unite all Toads into one nation.” Waluigi rewinds to “to un—”. The sentence swerves, but the declared goal is unity. The screen is still dark, Rivers is hogtied, and Waluigi is not calling that a settled political plan. Keep rolling.

PEN. TRIP. LIGHTS OUT. Waluigi is labeling the action because the shot has become an instruction diagram for losing a room.

sections.heading: THE DARKNESS HAS A VERY SPECIFIC ARCHIE IMPRESSION
sections.body:
Markop asks why Rivers lied. Rivers answers, “Lying is power, that's why, silly. These Toads are well within my grasp.” Waluigi leans toward the projector. That is a confession of technique delivered as though it were a tea recommendation. Rivers says he would not say it aloud where people could see him. Markop points out that people can still hear. Rivers doubts they are clever enough to deduce who is speaking. “Yup,” Markop says. “Watch this.”

A voice in the dark shouts, “I AM ARCHIE MISER! HAHAHA! THE EVIL ONE!” A scream follows. Waluigi freezes the picture. The line is so loud it practically comes with its own lantern. The account says Zes T, the Knight, and Feyward Dan can tell it is not Archie; everyone else thinks Archie is there. One guard is fairly sure Archie left before the lights went out. Waluigi looks at the empty screen, then at the audience. If the guard’s timing is right, the voice is doing a great deal of work with a person who may not be present. The tape does not give Waluigi permission to decide who performed it.

Markop says he can clearly see Rivers is lying. Someone calls, “Fireball! Fireball!” Then the transcript names the next speaker as Narjio: “You're going to jail. I'm bringing you to jail.” Rivers asks, “Under whose authority?” The answer is “The Legion.” Markop thinks that is no good answer. Waluigi taps the side of the projector. The dark-room investigation has moved from a pen, to a fake Archie voice, to a jurisdictional argument about the Legion. This is a lot of plot for one blackout.

Markop puts Rivers on his back and carries him toward the engine room. He says he cannot believe Rivers did this to all these Toads. Waluigi lets the shot travel with them. The carried man is still talking, the carrier is still walking, and nobody has explained how a place that was empty a moment ago is about to contain another group. The picture reaches the engine room. Waluigi does not cut ahead. Whatever is there has to enter the frame first.

ARCHIE? NOT ARCHIE? IN THE DARK? Waluigi is holding the frame still until the names stop trying to solve the voice for him.

sections.heading: THE TOAD RANGERS HAVE THEIR OWN VERSION OF JUSTICE
sections.body:
The engine room contains the Toad Rangers. One Toad has a gunshot wound and appears to be bleeding badly. Markop asks, “Didn't you guys kidnap her?” A Ranger objects, “You say ‘you guys’ like we're all the same.” Markop clarifies, “I meant, like, you people.” Waluigi pauses on the Ranger’s face. This is not a good moment to treat a group as one person, especially while asking that group about a kidnapping. The correction is short. It still lands.

The wound begins to mend by itself. Markop heals the wounded Toads, but the account does not give the Rangers’ later condition. Waluigi keeps the picture on what it shows: healing begins, Markop helps, the outcome beyond that is not announced. No glowing checkmark pops onto the screen. The Rangers say they want their own kind of justice, unlike Rivers. Then they point to Rivers on Markop’s back and call him their leader.

Markop insists Rivers is a liar and tells them not to trust him. The Rangers’ answer and Markop’s answer do not line up, and Waluigi will not make one of them disappear by turning up the projector volume. Markop has had enough and leaves. The sequence ends there: Rivers was carried in, the Rangers still recognize him, and the wounded Toads’ condition remains open. Waluigi lets the image breathe for half a second. It is a pause, not a conclusion.

Then the reel does something strange. The transcript gives this sequence once under “The Past,” labels the next block “The Future,” and plays the same past sequence again. Waluigi reaches for the rewind button, checks that the footage is identical, and stops the operator from counting a second blackout, a second hogtie, or a second group of Rangers. This is the same encounter repeated in the account, not a new trip to the engine room. Waluigi is not multiplying Toad Rangers because somebody pasted twice. He returns to the first frame of breakfast. The bread is still there. The question is still how to get the ship back.

SAME PAST. SAME BLACKOUT. SAME RANGERS. Waluigi is not pressing replay a second time just because the page did.

sections.heading: TOTAL CONTROL ARRIVES BEFORE THE EGGS
sections.body:
Back at the stall, a server in a maid’s dress brings Archie a drink. The account describes the server as a Toad. Remi wonders if the server is a man, because the voice sounds like Archie played on fast-forward. Waluigi listens to the imagined playback speed and does not make a ruling about the server’s identity. Archie cannot tell Remi. The drink is on the table, and the ship is still on everyone’s mind.

Someone says, “The problem started when they tried to steal our ship.” Remi suggests talking with “theo ther friends” about it; Waluigi hears the words as written and does not summon a new person named Theo. The phrase is unclear. Remi says she wants total control of the ship. Somebody repeats “total control.” Waluigi glances at the empty chair, because this is exactly when a meal stops being a meal and becomes a meeting with plates.

Green T says, “I got a deal for you.” Archie asks, “Can we talk about this somewhere else? People are staring.” Waluigi tilts the projector toward the diners. They are, in fact, looking over. A restaurant full of people has noticed that the conversation contains a ship, total control, and an offer. The room has ears. The room also has eggs.

The second course arrives: soft-boiled eggs, three minutes exactly, iron cups; thick-cut smoked sausage, boar and venison; turnip, parsnip, and winter-potato hash fried in rendered fat; stewed apples with one clove. Waluigi reads the menu like an announcer at a championship. Archie inspects the food for poison. Remi is already eating. That is the whole contrast: one person checks the breakfast, one person has begun breakfast. Green T sits down and orders green tea. Waluigi points at the cup. The transcription writes “green T”; the scene has Green T ordering tea. Nobody at this table needs another Green T. The course is served; the conversation is not over.

TOTAL CONTROL. A DEAL. PEOPLE STARING. NOW SERVE THE EGGS. Waluigi is stunned that the plates are the most orderly participants.

sections.heading: DEFINE FRIENDS, THEN ASK THE SERVER HER NAME
sections.body:
Archie tells Remi she cannot run off with strangers or take reckless risks. Markop and the three Toads who sacrificed limbs to keep her safe are not a reason to forget her friends for free candy. Waluigi nods at the warning and then watches the definition arrive. Remi says, “I go off with friends.” Archie asks, “Define friends.” She says, “They were pretty nice.” Archie replies, “They were being polite. You can't go with them just because they were polite.”

Remi says that is how people make friends, and they could always use more. Archie concedes the point, then warns that some friends could be using them. Remi says, “See? They led us here and they led us home to the ship. We need to take it back.” Archie whispers, “Why say this in the restaurant?” Remi answers, “No one listens anyway.” Waluigi swivels the projector toward the next table. The diners are still looking. Archie points out that he is whispering and she is not, then asks, “Keep your voice down, pretty please.” The politeness is doing its best. The volume is not.

After the second course, Archie turns to the maid. “Excuse me, miss, who are you? You haven't introduced yourself yet.” She says, “Oh, well, it's me,” and removes her disguise. Archie asks, “Who are you?” Remi asks, “Can you get us your drinks?” Waluigi stops the frame on the missing name. The woman does not supply one. The scene says her face looks like X.O.; resemblance is not an introduction, and Waluigi is not adding a biography to the pause.

The screen gives us a server, a removed disguise, a question with no name in reply, and Remi asking for drinks again. It does not identify the woman. Waluigi has written NOTHING on the card where an answer might go and underlined it twice. The question can stay open. The person at the table is still unnamed, and the plates are still on the table.

FRIENDS. STRANGERS. POLITENESS. VOLUME. Waluigi is watching a quiet conversation fail to become quiet.

sections.heading: MARKOP TRIES TO TAKE A SPEAKER THROUGH TOWN
sections.body:
Markop is on his way when two people stop him. They introduce themselves as Bystiall and Hargram and ask for Rivers. Markop says he is not giving Rivers up. They say they will take care of Rivers and raise their weapons. Waluigi leans toward the screen. Two names, two raised weapons, and one person being carried between competing claims. The account does not give Bystiall another identifying detail, and “Hargram” does not come with a surname here. Waluigi cannot turn a first name into a full introduction just because the scene has become tense.

Markop runs. He cannot believe he is being attacked in the middle of the street. Waluigi runs the camera with him, not ahead of him. There is no statement that Markop is wounded, no report that he fights back, and no view of where he goes after running. The only direction in the scene is away from the weapons. That is enough movement for one shot.

Archie sees Markop go and shrugs: “Hmm. Looks like it was Markop. We'll check up on him after breakfast.” He says he has to go, then eats quickly. Waluigi gestures at the frame. This is a remarkably practical response to a man being chased through town while carrying a Speaker: finish breakfast, then check. The sentence is funny because it lands exactly where it lands; Waluigi does not need to add a heroic rescue that is not on screen.

The street scene stops with Markop running and the two pursuers’ identities still only the names they supplied. Rivers’ destination is not shown. The Toad Rangers’ belief that he is their leader has not been withdrawn, and Markop’s belief that he is lying has not changed. Waluigi holds the image on the empty patch of street after the runners leave it. The frame does not tell us who now has Rivers. It tells us Markop was carrying him and then ran. No extra scene appears when Waluigi squints at the blank wall.

TWO NAMES. TWO WEAPONS. ONE PERSON CARRIED. NO DESTINATION. Waluigi holds the frame exactly where the picture stops telling him more.

sections.heading: THE BILL, THE WRAPPER, AND THE MISSING FIFTH TOAD
sections.body:
The unnamed woman quotes Archie twenty gold. The account says the amount was originally fifty and wonders whether the rest is on the house; the screen does not settle the bill. Waluigi points at the space where the receipt would be and finds no receipt. That is not a reason to invent one. The woman gives Remi a chocolate wrapper. Archie carries Remi across his back, her stomach against his shoulder and her upper body forward. Waluigi studies the pose. This is a very specific way to transport a person and a very ordinary way to keep a conversation moving while somebody is being carried. The wrapper is in Remi’s hand; the final price is still unclear.

Then someone asks, “Why do they want you so bad?” The answer is not reliably assigned to a speaker. It begins, “I did organize the initial assault.” Waluigi freezes the frame at the pronoun and writes a large question mark in the margin of the screen. He can follow the speech without pretending to know whose mouth said it.

The account describes the Legion’s flamethrower burning people to a crisp, distinguishes it from Archie’s fireball, and says five Toads died. Four names arrive: Toad Burt, Toad Lurt, Toad Eurt, and Toad Smurt. Waluigi counts them on his fingers. One, two, three, four. The spoken total is five. The frame supplies no fifth name, and Waluigi’s fingers are not a witness list.

The speaker says it was “for a better Toad future, I guess,” that there was nothing to live for in the Midlands, and regrets not staying at Port Toadstool before the group ventured onto a Toad-trafficking airship. The account does not repair the speaker attribution or identify the unnamed fifth Toad. Waluigi will not do either with a dramatic zoom. A chocolate wrapper, a disputed bill, a carried passenger, five deaths, four names. That is already enough material for one lunch break, and the picture has not reached the next interruption.

FIVE DEAD. FOUR NAMES. ONE UNKNOWN. Waluigi is counting again and does not have a fifth finger that can supply a name.

sections.heading: A PISTOL, A POLITICAL CLAIM, AND DAYCARE
sections.body:
A gun cocks. Green T approaches. Archie says the party has just returned from another dimension and is not going to kill people merely because killing is part of someone else’s life. Waluigi does not turn that paraphrase into a quotation. Green T says Rivers is a liar and needs to die. Then Green T gives his account: Speaker L became sick; Rivers, as vice-president, took over; when Speaker L did not recover, Rivers cast him aside. Waluigi keeps the screen on the speaker. A claim is being made; the scene has not supplied an independent answer.

Markop asks whether Speaker L was arrested and who turned him in. Archie says they found Speaker L and were bringing him back to the ship. Green T says Rivers turned him in. Someone accuses Rivers of betraying his own people. The answer is, “Toads are more than a people. We are the Toads.” Waluigi sits back. That line is a declaration of belonging, not a receipt for who gets to command the ship. The disagreement stays right there on the screen.

Archie reaches for Green T’s pistol. Green T dodges and slaps Archie’s hand with a rifle. “Don't you try anything. I'll use your third eye as an apple target.” Waluigi’s hand goes to the projector remote, not his own face. Markop says the Toads are being taken advantage of. Archie agrees they might be, but says the Toads do not want the party back, even after being saved; he calls them ungrateful and suggests leaving them as their own people, even as fugitives. Green T says the Toads need a competent, powerful leader like Archie. Archie says they want a charismatic Toad, not him.

Markop asks, “So the Toads are racist?” Archie answers, “In a way.” Markop says he has no clue and that they need a ship; perhaps another one, but first they need money. Then he asks Remi, “What about you? What do you think?” Remi says, “Thinking is too hard.” Green T calls her a liability and suggests daycare. Archie asks whether she wants to stay or go. Remi says, “Daycare sounds kinda fun,” then decides it would be boring anyway. Waluigi will concede one physical fact: the breakfast happened, and the meal did not disappear while everyone argued. He snaps back to the last frame: the ship is not back, Rivers’ custody is not shown, and Remi stays with the party for now. WAH!

PISTOL. RIFLE. THIRD EYE. APPLE TARGET. DAYCARE. Waluigi is now watching breakfast host an entire committee. NOT SETTLED. NOT RETURNED. NOT DECIDED.
